text:
Maria K.: Quick sync — ran the 60-day hosted demand sim and we have a non-trivial mismatch vs committed supply in eu-west1. Forecast shows ~14% GPU-hour shortfall for the p8/p10 mix if traffic grows as expected. Need rebalancing plan + cost check.

Lee H.: Do you have the raw numbers? 14% sounds significant but depends on absolute hours.

Maria K.: Yeah, summary below (rounded):
- eu-west1 demand (60d): 48k GPU-hours
- eu-west1 committed: 41.5k GPU-hours
- shortfall: ~6.5k GPU-hours (~14%)
- us-central is +8k spare hours on committed pools (mostly p8)

Aj Patel: Thanks. Two quick things — 1) are those numbers accounting for planned canary/rollouts? 2) any reservations currently pinned to clusters that are not movable?

Maria K.: Canary buffers accounted for (we reserve extra 2k hours globally). Some committed slots are tied to dedicated accounts for enterprise customers (approx 1.2k in eu-west1) so true movable amount is ~5.3k short.

Sophie G.: Finance flagged a separate billing delta last week — they saw committed utilization higher than reported in our billing pipeline for eu-west1. Could be an ingestion lag. I can re-run the query if helpful.

Maria K.: Yes please. Quick query I used (bigquery):
```sql
SELECT region,
  SUM(used_gpu_hours) AS used,
  SUM(committed_gpu_hours) AS committed
FROM billing.gpu_usage
WHERE date >= '2026-04-01' AND date < '2026-06-01'
GROUP BY region;
```

InfraBot: Automated alert — Reserved utilization >95% in eu-west1-p10 pool for last 7 days. Ticket created: INFRA-4892.

Lee H.: If us-central has +8k spare, could we do a soft-commit transfer (move reservation from us-central -> eu-west1) for p8 and then rely on cross-region routing for short term? Need to check latency differences and contractual impact.

Aj Patel: Two deployment constraints: cross-region move will change network egress for some enterprise customers — we need opt-in from customer-configured routes. Also, reassigning committed SKUs could incur early-termination or reallocation fees depending on the cloud vendor. I pulled the vendor policy: reallocation is allowed but charge applies if change frequency >2 per quarter.

Sophie G.: On the billing delta — I re-ran the pipeline and found ~0.7% undercount in usage ingestion for eu-west1 for April. Not enough to explain the whole shortfall but worth correcting. I'll file a follow-up with data-eng (ticket DATA-3321).

Maria K.: Proposal:
- Short term (0-14d): enable cross-region routing fallback to us-central reserved pool for non-enterprise traffic; tighten prefix caching to reduce token-hours by ~2%-3% (saves ~1.4k hours).
- Medium term (15-45d): soft-reallocate 2.5k p8-equivalent from us-central to eu-west1 committed pool (coordinate with vendor & finance).
- Long term (45-90d): increase reserved capacity in eu-west1 in next commit cycle if usage trend holds.

Lee H.: +1 for the fallback idea. How do we implement routing? We can add a routing policy rule:
```
route_policy {
  match: region == "eu-west1" && customer_tier != "enterprise"
  prefer: local_pool
  fallback: us-central:pool-p8
  max_fallback_latency_ms: 40
}
```

Aj Patel: I'll validate enterprise route opt-ins and vendor fees today. If fees are <10% of the monthly committed cost, soft-realloc looks reasonable.

Sophie G.: I'll continue with data-ingestion fix and send revised numbers by EOD.

Maria K.: Action items:
- Aj: check vendor reallocation policy & estimated fees (ETA: 6h)
- Sophie: final ingestion numbers + DATA ticket (ETA: EOD)
- Lee: implement routing policy as temporary fallback (ETA: 24h)
- Maria: update forecasting model with corrected ingestion numbers and re-run cost impact (ETA: 48h)

Lee H.: I can start a small runbook for the routing fallback and test in staging tonight. Will ping when ready. :thumbsup: 

InfraBot: Reminder — INFRA-4892 pending. Linking to thread.

Maria K.: Thanks all. If the ingestion fix reduces the gap materially we can avoid reallocation. Otherwise we proceed with fallback + partial soft-realloc. Will post numbers after the re-run.

Lee H.: Noted. Please @Maria K. when you post the new forecast so I can schedule the routing rollout windows.

Aj Patel: FYI I checked the vendor policy: first reallocation in quarter is free, second triggers a 5% fee. I will document cost math in the ticket.

Sophie G.: Updated numbers: revised shortfall now ~4.6k GPU-hours (after ingestion correction and cache savings). Sending CSV to #finance.

Maria K.: OK that's much better. Going ahead with routing fallback only and holding off on reallocation unless we see another upward trend. Closing loop after next 7-day check. :white_check_mark:
